<h>Invitatorium</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Jubilémus Deo, * Salutári nostro.
<r>Ant.</r> Jubilémus Deo, * Salutári nostro.
<c>V</c>eníte, exsultémus Dómino, jubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem ejus in confessióne, et in psalmis jubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Jubilémus Deo, * Salutári nostro.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Salutári nostro.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus ejus <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus ejus, et oves páscuæ ejus.
<r>Ant.</r> Jubilémus Deo, * Salutári nostro.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem ejus audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Salutári nostro.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus jurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Jubilémus Deo, * Salutári nostro.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Salutári nostro.

De Osée Prophéta
<r>Osee 4:1-3</r>
<n>1</n> Audíte verbum Dómini, fílii Israël, quia judícium Dómino cum habitatóribus terræ: non est enim véritas, et non est misericórdia, et non est sciéntia Dei in terra.
<n>2</n> Maledíctum, et mendácium, et homicídium, et furtum, et adultérium inundavérunt, et sanguis sánguinem tétigit.
<n>3</n> Propter hoc lugébit terra, et infirmábitur omnis qui hábitat in ea, in béstia agri, et in vólucre cæli; sed et pisces maris congregabúntur.
<h>H</h>æc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>Q</c>uintodécimo Kaléndas Decémbris Luna duodevicésima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>N</h>eocæsaréæ, in Ponto, natális sancti Gregórii, Epíscopi et Confessóris, doctrína et sanctitáte illústris, qui propter signa atque mirácula, quæ cum multa Ecclesiárum glória perpetrávit, Thaumatúrgus est appellátus.
<h>H</h>elpíthi, in Saxónia, item natális sanctæ Gertrúdis, Vírginis, ex Ordine sancti Benedícti, quæ dono revelatiónum clara éxstitit. Ipsíus tamen festívitas prídie hujus diéi celebrátur.
<h>I</h>n Palæstína sanctórum Mártyrum Alphǽi et Zachǽi, qui primo anno persecutiónis Diocletiáni, post multa torménta, capitálem senténtiam subiére.
<h>C</h>órdubæ, in Hispánia, sanctórum Mártyrum Acíscli et Victóriæ germanórum, qui, in eádem persecutióne, Diónis Prǽsidis jussu sævíssime cruciáti sunt, et illústri passióne corónas a Dómino meruérunt.
<h>A</h>lexandríæ sancti Dionýsii Epíscopi, summæ eruditiónis viri, qui, multis confessiónibus clarus et pro passiónum tormentorúmque diversitáte magníficus, plenus diérum Conféssor quiévit, Valeriáni et Galliéni Imperatórum tempóribus.
<h>A</h>ureliánis, in Gállia, sancti Aniáni Epíscopi, cujus mortem in conspéctu Dómini pretiósam mirácula crebra testántur.
<h>I</h>n Británnia sancti Hugónis Epíscopi, qui, ex Mónacho Carthusiáno ad Ecclésiam Lincolniénsem regéndam vocátus, multis cláruit miráculis, et sancto fine quiévit.
<h>T</h>urónis, in Gállia, sancti Gregórii Epíscopi.
<h>F</h>loréntiæ sancti Eugénii Confessóris, qui fuit Diáconus beáti Zenóbii, ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopi.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.53d0c7a97e:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>N</c>ovember 17th 2027, the 18th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Neo-Caesarea, in Pontus, (about the year 270,) holy Gregory, Archbishop of that see, who was famous for teaching and holiness, and who came to be called the Wonder-worker, on account of the great signs and wonders which he worked to the great glory of the churches.
<h>A</h>t Helfta, in Saxony, (in the year 1334,) the holy Virgin Gertrude, of the Order of St. Benedict, eminent for her gift of revelations, whose feast is kept upon the day before.
<h>I</h>n Palestine, the holy martyrs Alphaeus and Zacchaeus, who were put to death after suffering many torments, in the first year of the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.
<h>A</h>t Cordova, the holy brother and sister Acisclus and Victoria, both martyrs, who in the same persecution by Diocletian aforesaid, were most cruelly tortured by command of the President Dion, and earned crowns of glory from the hand of the Lord.
<h>A</h>t Alexandria, holy Denys, Bishop (of that see,) a man of great learning, and glorious on account of his many confessions and his diverse sufferings and torments, who at length fell asleep in the Lord, full of days but still a Confessor, in the time of the Emperors Valerian and Gallienus, (in the year 265.)
<h>A</h>t Orleans, (in the year 453,) holy Anian, Bishop (of that see,) the preciousness of whose death, in the sight of the Lord, is attested by many miracles.
<h>I</h>n England, holy Hugh, Bishop of Lincoln. He was a Charter House Monk, who was called to rule the Church of Lincoln, was famous for many miracles, and died an holy death, (in the year 1200.)
<h>A</h>t Tours, (in the year 595,) holy Gregory, Bishop (of that see.)
<h>A</h>t Florence, the holy Confessor Eugene, a Deacon of blessed Zenobius, Bishop of that see.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
